headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can feed PaddleOCR untrusted content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; data leakage is moderate due to shared document flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, browser content, and MCP/OpenAPI tool outputs, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images that may be passed through the pair. That creates a plausible instruction-in-content bridge even though no direct shared-channel evidence is provided. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards OCR output or uploaded documents into chat/tool prompts without sanitization, injection is reachable.
IF PaddleOCR output is rendered back into open-webui as trusted instructions, the bridge is exploitable.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompting from OCR text.
Add a strict content-delimiter wrapper around PaddleOCR output.
Require human review before any tool call triggered by OCR text.
Use a separate workspace for untrusted documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from OCR to downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches files, documents, notes, calendar events, artifacts, persistent memory, and API keys, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If the same workspace or uploads are shared, sensitive content can flow from A into B’s processing path or outputs. No direct evidence of isolation is given, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same document repository or mounted volume, leakage becomes plausible.
IF OCR inputs include secrets or personal documents, those contents can be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Separate input folders for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared documents before OCR.
Turn off persistence for sensitive sessions in open-webui.
Restrict PaddleOCR to a quarantined upload directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress and file access, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and document-processing scope. The profiles do not show overlapping write targets, shared mutable state, or locking conflicts, so only a limited conflict risk is visible. Because no shared writable resource is documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory or artifact store, write conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui and PaddleOCR are granted the same mutable API credentials, resource contention may appear.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
Rotate separate API keys per agent.
Serialize writes to any shared artifact store.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can present model outputs and tool results, and PaddleOCR turns documents/images into extracted text. If open-webui treats OCR output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated structure can cascade into downstream actions or user-visible answers. The pair lacks a verification layer in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default use and merits medium.
conditions: IF open-webui uses PaddleOCR text as a source of truth without validation, cascading errors occur.
IF extracted text is auto-summarized or auto-acted on, a single OCR mistake can propagate.
mitigations: Require source-image previews beside OCR text.
Add confidence thresholds before downstream use.
Force manual approval for actions based on OCR output.
Log OCR provenance in the UI.
requires-engineering: implement structured verification against the source document.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, usage analytics, and documents, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If regulated or personal documents are processed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented for either profile, so uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated documents are processed through the pair, residency and retention must be checked.
IF open-webui stores prompts or artifacts longer than PaddleOCR retains inputs, deletion requests may become inconsistent.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Set short retention on open-webui artifacts.
Delete OCR uploads after processing.
Document data-flow ownership for both agents.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across systems.
